source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine Fuel - Fuel Pump, p.6M-15

procedures.title: Fuel pump: inspect
steps: Check that the pump mounting bolts and the inlet and outlet connections are tight.
notes: The diaphragm pump is driven off a camshaft eccentric; on V8s a push rod between the eccentric and the pump rocker arm works it (see figure 1P in the manual). It is serviced only as a complete assembly.

procedures.title: Fuel pump: test
steps: Test with the pump on the engine and fuel in the tank.
Tighten loose line connections and check the lines for bends or kinks.
Disconnect the fuel pipe at the carburetor and the distributor-to-coil primary wire so the engine cranks without firing; hold a container at the pipe end and crank a few turns.

If little or no fuel comes out, the pipe is clogged or the pump has failed: before pulling the pump, disconnect the pipes at the tank and pump outlet, blow them through with an air hose, reconnect and retest.
If flow is good, attach a pressure gauge to the open end of the pump-to-carburetor pipe and run the engine at about 450-1,000 rpm on the fuel in the bowl.
A good pump holds pressure within spec and steady across 450-1,000 rpm; replace it if pressure is low, high, or changes much with speed.
notes: The tank-to-pump line is the suction side and pump-to-carburetor the pressure side; pressure-side leaks drip fuel, while suction-side leaks only show up as reduced delivery.
CAUTION: when cranking remotely at the starter, disconnect the primary distributor lead at the coil negative post and have the ignition switch ON, or the switch grounding circuit will be damaged.

procedures.title: Fuel pump: remove
steps: Disconnect the inlet and outlet pipes at the pump.
Remove the mounting bolts, pump and gasket.
V8, if the push rod must come out: on 427 (396) engines remove the pipe plug and push rod; on 327 (302/307/350) engines remove the fuel pump adapter, gasket and push rod.

procedures.title: Fuel pump: install
steps: V8, if the push rod was removed: refit it along with the pipe fitting or fuel pump adapter, using gasket sealer on the gasket or fitting.
